final_answer: Hypothesis: Increased education expenditure is positively associated with higher human capital (as indicated by school enrollment rates) and economic output (as indicated by GNI per capita and exports of goods and services). This relationship is statistically significant, as evidenced by the moderate positive correlations (approximately 0.586) and the positive coefficients obtained from the multiple linear regression analysis. The context of this hypothesis is the analysis of data from Sub-Saharan Africa and Lower Middle Income Countries (LMC) from 1975 to 2015. The variables chosen are education expenditure (from the Adjusted_savings_education_expenditure_percentage_of_GNI.csv dataset), school enrollment (from the School_enrollment_primary_percentage_gross.csv and School_enrollment_secondary_percentage_gross.csv datasets), and economic output (from the GNI_per_capita_constant_2015_USdollar.csv and Exports_of_goods_and_services_annual_percentage_growth.csv datasets). The positive relationship between these variables suggests that increased education expenditure contributes to higher human capital and economic output.
